scenes: Your watch measures. Nura shows the working.
Recovery compares last night with your own previous twenty-eight nights. Open it to see heart-rate variability, sleeping heart rate, and sleep, with the weights shown.
Sleep looks beyond the hours. Duration, regularity, and interruptions make up most of the score. Estimated sleep need also reflects strain, sleep debt, and naps.
Strain tracks how much work your heart did, on a zero-to-twenty-one scale. Harder minutes count more. Open a workout to inspect heart-rate zones and training load.
Your health score brings together cardio fitness, activity, sleep, and resting heart rate. The contribution of each part is visible, for a day or a longer period.
Cardio puts your estimated oxygen capacity in context for your age and sex, alongside heart-rate trends.
The target planner estimates which changes would move your score, using your own numbers. The assumptions stay visible.
Body Age takes a longer view, using six-month averages. Unpack the factors, follow the monthly trend, and treat it as a habits estimate.
The method stays open: formulas, weights, research, and limitations. You can inspect the reasoning behind the number.
